summary: DNP3 (IEEE 1815) is a SCADA/OT master-outstation protocol dominant in North American electric/water utilities. Base protocol has no authentication (Secure Authentication SAv2/SAv5 is an optional bolt-on rarely enabled), so any reachable outstation exposes physical process data and control functions (Operate/Direct Operate, Cold/Warm Restart) to anyone on the link. A DNP3 device on a corporate/DMZ segment is by itself a segmentation gap. recce has zero coverage today — port 20000 is missing from svcdetect and serviceenum and there is no services/dnp3.py — so a DNP3 outstation shows up in a scan as an unlabeled port and gets no per-service enumeration. The recce opportunity is a read-only probe modelled on modbus.py that positively identifies DNP3 via the 0x0564 link-layer sync + CRC-16-DNP, reads Class 0 static data (FC1, g60v1) to prove liveness, extracts vendor/product/firmware/site-name from Group 0 device attributes, harvests the outstation source address + master DFC/DIR bits, and flags reachability, missing SA, and any restart-bit / device-trouble IIN state — all without ever emitting a write, operate, restart, or unsolicited-toggle frame.

existing_coverage.notes: Zero coverage. Port 20000 is absent from recce/services/svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES (Modbus 502 is present via services/modbus.py, S7 102 via inferred label, but nothing for DNP3/20000). Absent from recce/services/serviceenum.py _PORT and _NAME (no dnp3 script mapping). No recce/services/dnp3.py exists. No dnp3 script under recce/scripts/. Full case-insensitive grep for dnp3/1815 across recce/ returns nothing.

capabilities.name: dnp3_link_layer_id
capabilities.description: Confirm the port speaks DNP3 by sending a Data-Link REQUEST_LINK_STATUS (FC9) or reading the 0x05 0x64 sync + CRC-16-DNP on the reply — positive protocol ID, distinguishes DNP3 from arbitrary services on 20000/tcp.
capabilities.notes: Frame layout: 0x05 0x64 | LEN | CTRL | DST(2 LE) | SRC(2 LE) | CRC(2). CRC-16-DNP polynomial 0x3D65 over the header, then per-16-byte data block. Reuse this parser for every capability below.

capabilities.name: dnp3_read_class0_static
capabilities.description: Send Application FC1 (Read) with object header g60v1 (Class 0 data) to enumerate the outstation's static analog/binary/counter points and prove the device is a real DNP3 outstation, not a proxy.
capabilities.notes: This is the hint's recommended probe. Read-only, no side effects. Parse the response's object headers to count binary/analog/counter/frozen-counter groups (1, 30, 20, 21) — a real outstation always returns at least one.

capabilities.name: dnp3_device_attributes
capabilities.description: Read Group 0 device-attribute variations (240 SoftwareVersion, 242 DeviceManufacturersName, 243 DeviceLocation, 250 UserAssignedDeviceName, 252 SerialNumber) via FC1 to fingerprint vendor/firmware for CVE mapping.
capabilities.notes: Fills Port.product/version so the CVE mapper keys on it. g0v242 typically holds strings like 'SEL', 'GE Multilin', 'Siemens SICAM', 'Schweitzer'.

capabilities.name: dnp3_outstation_address_disclosure
capabilities.description: Extract the outstation source address (SRC field, 2 bytes LE) and destination address it accepted from any reply — needed for every subsequent DNP3 command and is often a per-substation identifier.
capabilities.notes: Address 0 = master default, 1-65519 = station addresses, 0xFFFD/E/F = broadcast. Try dst=1..16 (common), 100, 1024 if the default returns no response — many outstations reject frames for wrong addresses silently.

capabilities.name: dnp3_missing_secure_auth
capabilities.description: Confirm the outstation accepts an FC1 Read without an Authentication Request (g120vN) preceding it — proves IEEE 1815 §7 Secure Authentication (SAv2/SAv5) is not enforced.
capabilities.notes: Base DNP3 has no auth. SA is the only defense; if the outstation answers a plain Read it is running without it. Do NOT test with a WRITE — reachability of unauthenticated Read is already the finding.

capabilities.name: dnp3_iin_flags_parse
capabilities.description: Parse the 16-bit IIN (Internal Indications) field in every response and flag Device Restart (IIN1.7), Device Trouble (IIN1.6), Need Time (IIN1.4), Local Control (IIN1.5), and Config Corrupt (IIN2.5).
capabilities.notes: Device Restart bit indicates uptime reset since last CLEAR — an attacker who saw it before you did may have already issued FC13/14.

capabilities.name: dnp3_broadcast_response
capabilities.description: Send an FC1 Read to broadcast destination 0xFFFD (with confirmation) — an outstation that answers a broadcast leaks its address without any prior knowledge and permits sweep-style enumeration.
capabilities.notes: 0xFFFD requires application-layer confirmation, 0xFFFE requires DL confirmation, 0xFFFF no confirmation. Well-designed outstations ignore broadcast reads.

capabilities.name: dnp3_unsolicited_probe
capabilities.description: Listen briefly after link identification for unsolicited response frames (App Control UNS bit set) — an outstation configured for unsolicited reporting to a wrong/absent master will spray event data to whoever answers.
capabilities.notes: Do NOT send FC20/21/22 (Enable/Disable Unsolicited) — that changes device state. Just read for a few seconds after connect.

capabilities.name: dnp3_control_functions_supported
capabilities.description: Infer supported dangerous function codes (FC3 Select, FC4 Operate, FC5 Direct Operate, FC6 Direct Operate No Ack, FC13/14 Cold/Warm Restart, FC18 Stop Application) from the response to FC1 g60v1 without ever invoking them.
capabilities.notes: Never emit FC3/4/5/6/13/14/18 — those change plant state. Report their potential availability as risk context alongside dnp3_no_secure_auth.

capabilities.name: dnp3_udp_variant
capabilities.description: Repeat the link-layer probe on 20000/udp — DNP3-over-UDP is defined in IEEE 1815 §7.2 and is sometimes deployed on wireless SCADA links but often overlooked in firewall rules.
capabilities.notes: Single datagram, same 0x0564 frame. Reuse svcdetect's inferred label for 20000/udp.

capabilities.name: dnp3_svcdetect_registration
capabilities.description: Add 20000/tcp and 20000/udp to svcdetect.PORT_NAMES (label 'dnp3', 'DNP3 SCADA outstation (IEEE 1815)') so unlabeled scans no longer report the port as unknown.
capabilities.notes: Trivial two-line change. Also add 'dnp3' -> 'dnp3' to serviceenum._NAME and 20000 -> 'dnp3' to serviceenum._PORT so `recce services` emits the enum command for the port.

capabilities.name: dnp3_signature_bytes
capabilities.description: Add a servicefp signature for the 0x0564 start-bytes so nmap-captured servicefp on non-standard ports (e.g. DNP3 on 20001/20002 for multiple RTUs) also labels as DNP3.
capabilities.notes: Regex ^\x05\x64 in svcdetect._SIGNATURES. Very low FP rate — 0x0564 is a stable, unique sync.

capabilities.name: dnp3_delay_measurement
capabilities.description: Optionally send FC23 (Delay Measurement) to characterise round-trip time to the outstation — a benign read-only frame that also proves master-side timing works.
capabilities.notes: Purely informational, but useful as a second-source liveness check when g60v1 is empty on a spare device.

capabilities.name: dnp3_runbook_output
capabilities.description: Emit a per-target runbook of the safe-first tools a tester should run (nmap dnp3-info NSE, opendnp3 dnp3ctl, DNP3 dissector in Wireshark) mirroring modbus.py's runbook() pattern.
capabilities.notes: e.g. 'nmap -sU -sT -p 20000 --script dnp3-info', 'python3 -m pydnp3 read-class0 {ip}:20000 --dst 1'. Keeps the tool consistent with how modbus/mssql/etc surface next-step commands.

recommended_findings.title: DNP3 SCADA outstation reachable on the scanned network
DNP3 outstation accepts Read without Secure Authentication (IEEE 1815 §7)
DNP3 outstation responds to broadcast address 0xFFFD
DNP3 IIN flags indicate device restart / trouble / config corrupt
DNP3 unsolicited responses observed on connect (misconfigured event target)
Port 20000 unlabeled (missing svcdetect entry for DNP3)

cross_service_wire_candidates: vendor / product / firmware version from Group 0 device attributes (g0v240 SoftwareVersion, g0v242 DeviceManufacturersName, g0v250 UserAssignedDeviceName, g0v252 SerialNumber) — feeds Port.product/version and the CVE mapper for vendor-specific SCADA CVEs (SEL, GE Multilin, Schweitzer, Siemens SICAM, Schneider SCADAPack)
outstation user-assigned device name (g0v250) — hostname-like identifier, feeds known_hostnames and helps correlate the same RTU across masters and across engineering-workstation SMB shares

device location string (g0v243) — site name / substation identifier, justifies a NEW shared surface (known_sites / known_substations) that would let recce correlate DNP3 outstations with the DMS/SCADA HMI hostnames on the corporate side

outstation DNP3 source address (2-byte LE) — feeds a NEW shared surface (dnp3_addresses) so a second scan of the same subnet can reuse addresses rather than re-sweep, and so an engineering-workstation loot pass can cross-check DNP3 addresses embedded in project files

list of dangerous function codes the outstation appears to support (FC3/4/5/13/14/18) — feeds relay_targets style context so the attack-path builder can rank DNP3 outstations by blast radius (control-capable vs read-only IEDs)

whether Secure Authentication (g120) is enforced — a boolean that other services (engineering workstation, HMI web UI, historian) can use to prioritise credential harvesting where SA keys might be extractable
master address(es) the outstation ACKs frames from — leaks the SCADA master IP addressing plan, feeds known_hosts / known_masters for lateral movement targeting
implementation_notes: Model on recce/services/modbus.py exactly — same shape: is_dnp3(port), _build_*() PDU builders, _parse_*_response(), probe(), <service>_targets(), findings(), runbook(), findings_to_vulns() via svccommon, analyze() using svcprobe.iter_probe. Airgap-safe stdlib only (socket + struct). CRITICAL protocol quirks: (1) All Data-Link addresses are LITTLE-endian 2-byte, application layer is byte-oriented — do NOT reuse Modbus's '>H' packing globally. (2) CRC-16-DNP uses polynomial 0x3D65 (reflected 0xA6BC), computed over the 8-byte header alone, then over each 16-byte user-data block; a stub _crc_dnp() of ~15 lines suffices. (3) Frames larger than 16 bytes of user data need multiple CRC-bearing blocks — the FC1 g60v1 request fits in one block, but responses often do not, so the parser must strip CRCs every 18 bytes (16 data + 2 CRC). (4) Application layer adds an Application Control byte with FIR/FIN/CON/UNS/SEQ — set FIR=FIN=1, CON=0, UNS=0, SEQ rotates 0-15. (5) Transport layer adds one byte between DL header and app layer (FIN/FIR/SEQ 0-63) — easy to forget, breaks every reply. (6) Default src=1 (master), dst=1..10 (outstation) — try 1 first, then 2, 3, 4, 10, 100 if silent. (7) NEVER emit FC3 Select, FC4 Operate, FC5 Direct Operate, FC6 Direct Operate No Ack, FC13 Cold Restart, FC14 Warm Restart, FC15 Initialize Data, FC16 Initialize App, FC17 Start App, FC18 Stop App, FC20/21/22 (Enable/Disable/Assign Unsolicited), FC31 Save Config — these change plant state and can trip protection relays. Read-only means FC1 (Read), FC23 (Delay Measurement), and Data-Link FC9 (Request Link Status) only. (8) Register 20000/tcp + 20000/udp in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES, add 'dnp3' entry to serviceenum._NAME/_PORT, and add ^\\x05\\x64 signature to svcdetect._SIGNATURES in the same PR. (9) Add is_dnp3() variant check for stray ports (some deployments run multiple RTUs on 20001, 20002, ..., 20009 on the same IP — accept 20000-20009 range as a hint, but require a valid 0x0564 reply before labelling).
